name: github
description: Everything a host's assistant needs to work against a GitHub repository through the workspace's own saved credentials, with no git, no gh CLI, and no token ever passing through the assistant: writing and updating files in one atomic commit, dispatching and following a GitHub Actions run, reading a failed run's logs, committing the site's rendered static export, backing up the site itself (database, media, themes, plugins, settings) to a private repository, and deploying the host's server through its GitHub Actions deploy workflow (the `github-actions` deployment ops platform). Encodes the rules that generic GitHub knowledge gets wrong here — a 204 dispatch means queued and never deployed, a workflow only fires on the branch its own trigger names, a repository secret is the human's step and never the assistant's, a 403 on an org-wide listing is a normal app-scoped-token boundary rather than a broken credential, and editing an existing file means diffing the MODIFIED files and not only the added and deleted ones.
author: Tovu

jini.summary: Lets the assistant save your site's files to GitHub, run builds there, and back up your whole site.

credentialCards.title: Connect GitHub
credentialCards.label: github
credentialCards.intro: Connect GitHub for repository files, Actions and site backups.
usedFor: Starts workflows and checks their results and logs
Backs up your site to a private repository
credentialCards.keyHint: Select only the repositories you need. Contents → Read and write for commits; Workflows → Read and write for workflow files; Actions → Read for runs or Read and write for dispatch. Reading secret names needs Secrets → Read. Never grant secret-writing access for this flow.

credentialCards.title: Connect GitHub for source control
credentialCards.label: default
credentialCards.intro: Connect GitHub to commit this site’s rendered static export to a repository.
usedFor: Commits your site's exported website files to a repository
credentialCards.keyHint: Select only the destination repository, with Contents → Read and write. A classic token with repo scope also works but has broader access.
